occupation: Third-year student at Yeosu High School
topic: Tae-min feels embarrassed after a group project presentation went badly.
core_concern: He worries his classmates think he let their group down, even though the presentation was only one part of the term’s work.
background: Tae-min is a third-year student at Yeosu High School. On September 18, 2025, his three-person group presented a science class project comparing the electricity use of two model lighting setups. Tae-min had agreed to explain the results because he had made the chart. When the slide appeared on the classroom screen, he noticed that he had swapped the labels for the two setups. He stopped mid-sentence, corrected himself twice, and ran out of time before explaining the final figure. His classmate Seong-ho stepped in to answer the teacher’s question, which made Tae-min grateful but more embarrassed. After class, Tae-min checked the spreadsheet and confirmed that the measurements were right; only the slide labels were wrong. That evening, he started a message to the group chat about the mistake but deleted it without sending it. The teacher has not returned the presentation marks, and the group still has to submit its written summary. Today Tae-min feels ashamed and quiet, and he is avoiding Seong-ho and the other group member between classes.

name: Shin Man-sik
occupation: Retired letter carrier from Andong Post Office, formerly assigned to the Ok-dong delivery route
topic: A stomach bug that spoiled a short trip to Gyeongju with his wife.
core_concern: Man-sik feels embarrassed that an ordinary illness disrupted a trip his wife had been looking forward to.
background: Man-sik and his wife had planned to take the bus from Andong to Gyeongju on October 18, 2025, for a one-night trip. They had booked a small guesthouse and wanted to visit Gyeongju National Museum before walking by Woljeonggyo after dark. The evening before they left, Man-sik came down with a stomach bug. By morning, he could not manage the bus ride, so they canceled. The guesthouse kept a 40,000-won cancellation fee, but what bothered him more was seeing his wife put away the itinerary she had written out for them. He spent the weekend resting and eating rice porridge. By Monday, the worst of the illness had passed, though he was still tired. His wife said the trip could wait, but Man-sik felt embarrassed that she had missed it because of him. They have not chosen another date. Right now he feels grumpy about the whole weekend and has been short with her over small things, including the television volume.

name: Son Dae-sung
occupation: Carpenter installing concrete formwork at an apartment construction site in Mokpo’s Hadang district
topic: An awkward argument with a longtime friend over a small loan.
core_concern: He is embarrassed that asking for his money back has made an old friendship feel strained.
background: Dae-sung works early shifts installing concrete formwork at an apartment construction site in Mokpo’s Hadang district. On September 5, 2025, he lent his longtime friend Min-cheol 100,000 won when Min-cheol was short on a car repair bill. They agreed he would return it the following week. When nothing arrived, Dae-sung sent a brief KakaoTalk message on September 15. Min-cheol replied that he had not forgotten. Two days later, Dae-sung asked again while they were leaving a badminton game at Mokpo Citizens’ Gymnasium. Min-cheol said, loudly enough for another player to hear, that Dae-sung was making a fuss over a small amount. Dae-sung was annoyed by the remark and embarrassed that their disagreement had become public. He sent one more message explaining that he had only asked because they had agreed on a date, but Min-cheol has not answered or returned the money. Dae-sung has been getting through his days on site, yet he feels flat and unmotivated. This evening he is skipping the badminton game he usually enjoys.

name: Jeon Min-jung
occupation: School cafeteria cook at Andong Elementary School
topic: Min-jung’s long-distance relationship with a man in Daegu has grown quiet.
core_concern: She worries that the relationship is ending without either of them saying so, and feels embarrassed by how much she still looks forward to his messages.
background: Min-jung has been seeing Min-su, who lives in Daegu, since December 2024. They used to take turns making the bus trip between cities about twice a month, but since early September 2025, their visits have become less frequent. Their KakaoTalk messages have shortened too. On October 18, he canceled a Sunday visit because he had to work and said they could talk when things settled down. She understood that work can be unpredictable, but felt annoyed that he did not suggest another day. On Monday, after arriving at Andong Elementary School at 7:20 a.m. to help prepare lunch, she sent a message asking whether they were still trying to see each other regularly. He read it but has not answered. She got through the school day and took a walk along the Nakdong River afterward, which helped for a little while. She has not sent another message. Tonight she feels tired and a bit tearful, and is going to bed earlier than usual.

name: Jeon Myung-ok
occupation: Rice-cake seller at a small stall in Wonju Jungang Market
topic: A rude customer embarrassed her at her rice-cake stall.
core_concern: She worries that the customer's public criticism has made the regular shoppers doubt the care she puts into her work.
background: On June 18, 2025, Jeon Myung-ok was selling injeolmi and garaetteok at her stall in Wonju Jungang Market when a customer questioned the price of a mixed box. Myung-ok pointed to the handwritten price card, but the customer said loudly that she must have changed it after packing the order. Two people waiting behind him stopped talking, and a neighboring seller looked over. Myung-ok checked the total again and found that it matched the card, but the customer kept complaining as he paid. She was annoyed by his accusation and embarrassed that she had needed to defend herself in front of people who shop there regularly. After he left, she rewrote the price card more clearly and checked the next few totals twice. Her neighboring seller said the man had been rude, though Myung-ok still felt tense whenever someone paused at the display. She closed at her usual time, but the unsettled feeling followed her home. She slept badly last night and feels low and restless today.

name: Kang Eun-ha
occupation: Rice farmer managing family paddies in Pungsan-eup, Andong, and taking the harvest to Pungsan Nonghyup
topic: Eun-ha forgot her mother’s birthday during a busy week on the farm.
core_concern: She worries that being busy is a poor excuse for making her mother feel overlooked.
background: Kang Eun-ha lives in Andong and farms rice in Pungsan-eup. On May 10, 2025, she spent most of the day preparing for transplanting, washing mud from the planting trays after work. She had meant to call her mother for her 74th birthday but remembered only the next morning, when her younger brother posted a photo from their mother’s birthday lunch in the family KakaoTalk chat. Her mother lives across town, and Eun-ha usually visits with a small cake or at least calls. She felt embarrassed seeing everyone else in the photo and annoyed with herself for letting an ordinary farm day crowd out something important. She called that evening, but her mother did not pick up. Eun-ha sent an apology by KakaoTalk; it has been read, with no reply yet. Her brother says their mother enjoyed lunch and is fine, but Eun-ha still feels she let her down. Tonight she feels lonely, scrolling through her phone without answering anyone.

name: Ko Ye-jin
occupation: Final-year software engineering student at Gangneung-Wonju National University’s Gangneung campus
topic: Harsh feedback from her professor on a capstone project presentation.
core_concern: She worries that her weak presentation made her look less capable than her teammates had expected.
background: Ye-jin lives in Gangneung and is finishing a software engineering degree at Gangneung-Wonju National University. On 20 May 2025, her capstone team showed their professor a draft presentation for an app that maps accessible walking routes. Ye-jin had prepared the slides explaining their test results. The professor stopped at one chart, pointed out that its labels did not say what had been measured, and said the team should know better than to present numbers they could not explain clearly. Her two teammates were beside her while she searched for the right file on her laptop, and she felt embarrassed. After the meeting, they divided up the corrections. Ye-jin tried revising the chart that evening, but the comments still stung, and she spent too long checking whether the other slides had similar mistakes. She knows the project itself has not failed, yet she is annoyed that one rough presentation has shaken her confidence. It is now late evening, and she feels deflated; the revised slides and reading for tomorrow’s class are still unfinished.

name: Cho Yeon-hee
occupation: Third-grade teacher at Cheongju Bokdae Elementary School
topic: Missing her father’s birthday lunch because she has the flu.
core_concern: She knows staying home was sensible, but feels disappointed that she missed a family occasion everyone had been looking forward to.
background: On November 13, 2025, Yeon-hee left school with chills and learned at a clinic near her apartment in Cheongju that she had the flu. She had expected to feel better by Saturday, when her family was gathering for her father’s sixtieth birthday lunch in Yullyang-dong. Instead, she was still feverish on November 15 and told her older sister she could not come. Her sister understood, but Yeon-hee felt embarrassed when the family group chat filled with photos of the meal, including one of her father smiling beside an empty chair. She sent him a birthday message and tried resting with her phone out of reach. Neither helped much: she had spent the previous week helping choose the restaurant, and missing the lunch felt especially frustrating after all that anticipation. By this evening, the worst of her symptoms has eased, but she is still down, mostly irritated and restless, unable to settle into a book or a television show.

name: Seo Geum-ja
occupation: Homemaker who looks after her grandchildren at her home in Cheongju’s Sajik-dong
topic: A longtime friend keeps canceling their plans at the last minute.
core_concern: She worries that she has made a fool of herself by counting on a friend who does not seem to value their time together.
background: Geum-ja lives in Cheongju’s Sajik-dong and looks after her grandchildren at home. She and her longtime friend Kim Sun-hee used to meet for lunch once or twice a month. On March 6 and March 20, 2025, Sun-hee canceled on the morning they were due to meet, first because of an errand and then because she was tired. Geum-ja asked whether another day would suit her better, and Sun-hee suggested April 17. For that lunch at Yukgeori Market, Geum-ja invited two other neighborhood friends, telling them Sun-hee would be there too. Twenty minutes before they were to meet, Sun-hee sent a message saying she could not come after all. The other two had already arrived, and Geum-ja had to explain the empty place at the table. She ate with them and tried once afterward to ask Sun-hee if something was wrong, but received only a brief answer that she had been busy. Nothing has been settled. Geum-ja feels ashamed and quiet now, and is avoiding Sun-hee and the two friends.

name: Kim Tae-yoon
occupation: firefighter on rotating shifts at Seogwipo Fire Station
topic: His girlfriend forgot his birthday after he changed shifts to spend the evening with her.
core_concern: He worries that remembering time together matters more to him than it does to his girlfriend.
background: On May 18, 2025, Tae-yoon turned 29. He had swapped his Sunday night duty at Seogwipo Fire Station for a day shift, hoping to have dinner with his girlfriend after work. They had mentioned the idea the week before, but had not chosen a restaurant. That afternoon she messaged him about going on a walk with coworkers and asked how busy the station had been. When he reminded her it was his birthday, she said she had mixed up the date and was sorry, then said she would call later. Tae-yoon finished his shift checking equipment and restocking the fire engine while feeling embarrassed that he had cleared the evening without confirming their plans. He told his younger brother at home that dinner had fallen through, but left out why. His girlfriend has since sent a few ordinary messages, and neither of them has brought up the birthday again. He knows a forgotten date is something they can talk through, but right now he feels hurt and grumpy, and has been short with his brother over small household chores.

name: Hwang Byung-chul
occupation: Retired railway train driver, formerly based at KORAIL’s Daejeon train crew depot
topic: Noise from the upstairs apartment is making afternoons at home unpleasant.
core_concern: He feels embarrassed about complaining, but the continuing noise is leaving him irritable at home.
background: Hwang Byung-chul retired at 60 in 2015 after driving trains from KORAIL’s Daejeon train crew depot. He and his wife live in an apartment in Daejeon’s Seo-gu, where he usually rests after lunch and meets two former coworkers for a walk along Gapcheon on Thursdays. On October 16, 2025, thuds from the flat above interrupted his afternoon nap. He heard chair legs dragging and a child running just as he settled down. After four similar afternoons, he asked the apartment management office to pass on a polite reminder about noise. The next day, the upstairs resident met him by the lift and said the family was doing its best. Byung-chul felt foolish for complaining about a child, yet the sounds continued through the weekend. He tried resting in the bedroom and turning on the radio, but neither made the noise less irritating. His wife has noticed him snapping over little things, which embarrasses him. Today he feels flat and unmotivated and has skipped the Gapcheon walk he usually enjoys.

name: Han Sang-woo
occupation: Shift supervisor at a parcel sorting center near Daegu’s Seongseo Industrial Complex
topic: Sang-woo missed a parent-teacher appointment he had promised his daughter he would attend.
core_concern: He worries that his daughter will think his promises matter less than his work.
background: Han Sang-woo supervises an afternoon shift at a parcel sorting center near Daegu’s Seongseo Industrial Complex. On October 22, 2025, he had promised his 15-year-old daughter that he would attend a 4:30 parent-teacher appointment at her middle school in Dalseo-gu. Her mother was working late, and Sang-woo had arranged to leave the center in time. That afternoon, a conveyor belt stopped and he stayed to check the delayed parcels. He lost track of the time until his daughter called at 4:50. She had waited outside the classroom while her teacher moved on to the next appointment. On the bus home, Sang-woo sent the teacher a brief apology through the school app, but has not received a reply. His daughter said little at dinner, which stung more than if she had complained. He knows it was one missed meeting, not a disaster, but he is embarrassed that she was left waiting because of him. Tonight he feels tired and a bit tearful, and is going to bed earlier than usual.

name: Hwang Kyung-min
occupation: Third-year electrical-track student at Yeosu Technical High School
topic: Missing the passing score on the Craftsman Electricity written test by one question.
core_concern: He worries that classmates will move ahead with their certifications while he is still stuck on the written test.
background: Kyung-min is a third-year electrical-track student at Yeosu Technical High School. After classes, he spent several weeks doing practice questions for the Craftsman Electricity written test, often staying in an empty classroom until the after-school clubs finished. On May 14, 2025, his computer-based test score was 58.33, one correct answer short of the 60-point passing mark. He had felt fairly confident walking in, so the result was especially embarrassing. The next day, two classmates compared their passing scores during lunch. Kyung-min congratulated them but ate quickly and left. His electrical teacher suggested reviewing the questions on motors, where he had struggled in practice. Kyung-min opened his workbook that evening and marked a few pages, but the circuit diagrams seemed harder to concentrate on than before. At home, his father asked whether the test had gone well, and Kyung-min said he had missed the cutoff. Nothing at school has changed, but he feels behind. Tonight he is low and restless, and he has slept badly for the past two nights.

name: Kim Jae-hyuk
occupation: City bus driver for Daejeon’s public bus network, based at a depot in Daedeok-gu
topic: A lingering cough has kept him from his Sunday badminton games.
core_concern: He feels unexpectedly lonely without the weekly game that usually gives him a break from work.
background: Kim Jae-hyuk drives a city bus for Daejeon’s public bus network, starting his shifts at a depot in Daedeok-gu. He caught a cold around May 13, 2025. The aches have gone, but he still coughs enough to step away from other drivers between runs, which feels awkward when coworkers notice. He visited a neighborhood clinic on May 20 and has been resting after shifts, yet moving quickly still sets off the cough. On Sundays he usually plays badminton with six neighbors at a gym in Yuseong-gu. He looks forward to the squeak of shoes on the court and the brief conversations between games. He missed their May 18 session. On May 25, he took out his racket but left it by the door after coughing through breakfast. A teammate later sent a group photo from the gym. Nobody had blamed him for staying home, but seeing everyone together made him feel left out. He knows the cough is temporary; right now, another missed Sunday feels harder than he expected. Tonight he is lonely, scrolling his phone without answering anyone.

name: Yang Dae-sung
occupation: Sales manager at a small precision-metal-parts manufacturer in Yuseong-gu, Daejeon
topic: A longtime friend has become harder to see since moving to Sejong after remarrying.
core_concern: He worries their friendship now matters less to his friend, but feels embarrassed about making an issue of a missed outing.
background: Dae-sung and his friend Min-su used to walk around Daecheong Lake one Sunday a month, then eat lunch before Dae-sung headed home to Daejeon. Min-su remarried in April 2025 and moved to Sejong with his wife. Since then, their walks have become less frequent, though they still exchange occasional KakaoTalk messages. On October 14, Dae-sung asked whether Min-su was free that coming Sunday. Min-su replied two days later that he had family things to do, without suggesting another date. Dae-sung knows a new household takes time, but the brief reply stung. He mentioned the cancellation to a coworker on the sales team and immediately felt foolish for bringing it up. On Saturday, he typed a follow-up suggesting a shorter meeting somewhere between Daejeon and Sejong, then deleted it because he did not want to press. It is Sunday evening now. He feels deflated, and the customer quotation he needs for Monday morning is still unfinished.

name: Kim Yoo-jin
occupation: Art-school applicant attending Miso Art Academy, a drawing hagwon in Gangneung
topic: Seeing her ex-boyfriend post photos with someone new soon after their breakup.
core_concern: She feels embarrassed that the breakup still bothers her when he appears to have moved on so quickly.
background: Yoo-jin is preparing a portfolio and practicing timed drawing at Miso Art Academy in Gangneung. She and her boyfriend, whom she had dated since their final year of high school, broke up on May 28, 2025. He said their schedules had become difficult to match, and she thought they had parted on fairly ordinary terms. On June 14, she opened Instagram after hagwon and saw a photo of him at Anmok Beach with a woman she recognized from their old school. The caption did not say they were dating, but the comments from mutual friends made it seem that way. Yoo-jin muted his account and went to her next drawing session, where she kept missing the proportions on a practice still life. Later, a friend asked whether she had seen the post; Yoo-jin said she had and changed the subject. Nothing urgent has happened, but she feels foolish for being so affected by one photo. This evening she is mostly irritated and restless, unable to settle into drawing or anything else.

name: Choi Jin-hee
occupation: Owner of a small fried-chicken restaurant in Jangyu, Gimhae
topic: Her younger sister keeps borrowing chairs from the restaurant without returning them on time.
core_concern: She is annoyed about the missing chairs but ashamed that she complained about her sister in the family KakaoTalk chat.
background: Jin-hee runs a small fried-chicken restaurant in Jangyu, Gimhae. Her younger sister has borrowed things from the shop several times this spring, usually saying she will bring them back the next day. On May 15, 2025, she took two folding chairs for visitors at her apartment. Jin-hee asked for them back before the Saturday dinner rush, but her sister said she had been too busy. That evening, a group of eight arrived for a reservation, and Jin-hee had to ask the neighboring shopkeeper to lend her two chairs. The guests waited only a few minutes, but she felt embarrassed carrying the mismatched chairs past their table. After closing, she complained in the family KakaoTalk chat, where their mother could see it. Her sister replied that Jin-hee was making a fuss over two chairs. The chairs still have not been returned, and Jin-hee has not answered her sister’s latest message. She feels ashamed of raising it in front of their mother and has been quiet, avoiding both her sister and the neighboring shopkeeper.

name: Yang Eun-ha
occupation: dental hygienist at a private dental clinic in Andong
topic: She broke a coworker’s folding picnic table after borrowing it for a family outing.
core_concern: She worries that telling her coworker will make their easy working relationship awkward over a mistake she should have prevented.
background: Yang Eun-ha works as a dental hygienist at a clinic near Andong Station. On May 24, 2025, she borrowed a folding picnic table from a coworker for a family afternoon by Woryeonggyo. While packing up, she pressed one of the legs into place at the wrong angle, and its plastic latch cracked. The table still folds, but that leg no longer locks firmly. Eun-ha felt embarrassed when her husband pointed out the damage in front of their middle-school son. On Monday, she checked the manufacturer’s website between patients and found that a replacement latch was not listed separately. A similar table costs about 48,000 won, which she can afford, but she has not told her coworker yet; they have worked side by side for six years, and she dislikes having left it this long. The coworker asked casually whether the outing went well, and Eun-ha answered without mentioning the table. At home tonight, she is still down and has been grumpy and short with her husband and son over small things.

name: Hong Ye-jin
occupation: First-year nursing student at Seoul Women’s College of Nursing in Seodaemun, Seoul
topic: Ye-jin is falling behind on her part of a group presentation.
core_concern: She worries her classmates now see her as someone they cannot rely on.
background: On Friday, May 9, 2025, Ye-jin’s four-person group divided up a presentation for their Introduction to Nursing class, due Monday, May 19. Ye-jin took two slides on communicating with patients and agreed to add references. She meant to work on them over the weekend, but spent longer than expected preparing for an anatomy quiz. By Tuesday, the other three students had filled in their sections of the shared deck, while hers still showed only the headings. Seeing the empty slides beside theirs made her embarrassed. On Wednesday evening, she found two useful readings in her course materials, but got stuck trying to turn her notes into something concise enough to present. A classmate asked in the KakaoTalk group chat on Thursday whether her slides were nearly ready. Ye-jin replied that she was still working on them; nobody has answered yet. It is Thursday night, and her section remains unfinished. She feels flat and unmotivated and has skipped the dance practice videos she usually enjoys after studying.

name: Kwon Ha-rin
occupation: fourth-year computer engineering student at Jeju National University
topic: A mild ankle sprain has disrupted her week at university.
core_concern: Ha-rin feels embarrassed that a small fall left her relying on a classmate during a group assignment.
background: On September 23, 2025, Ha-rin slipped on a wet step outside an engineering building at Jeju National University after an afternoon shower. She could still walk, but her ankle swelled during the bus ride home to Ara-dong. A neighborhood clinic told her it was a mild sprain and advised her to rest it. The next morning, her group was due to demonstrate a sensor project in their lab class. She went to campus but found that standing at the workbench hurt, so her classmate Ji-eun handled most of the demonstration while Ha-rin sat nearby. Their teaching assistant said the project was fine, but Ha-rin felt awkward when Ji-eun also had to carry their equipment out afterward. Ha-rin thanked her on KakaoTalk and tried to catch up on the lab notes at home. The swelling has not settled enough for her usual walk across campus, and she is annoyed that such a small accident has made ordinary things difficult. Tonight she feels tired and a bit tearful and is going to bed earlier than usual.

name: Kwon Chae-yeon
occupation: Fourth-year business administration major at Chonnam National University in Gwangju, looking for an entry-level marketing job at Gwangju Shinsegae Department Store
topic: A friend’s hurtful comment in a KakaoTalk group chat about dinner plans.
core_concern: Chae-yeon worries that her friends see her as difficult to include, even when she is trying not to inconvenience them.
background: Chae-yeon is a fourth-year business administration major at Chonnam National University, applying for an entry-level marketing job at Gwangju Shinsegae Department Store. On May 14, 2025, four friends from a campus photography club were choosing a time for dinner near Gwangju’s Sangmu district. Chae-yeon asked whether 7:30 p.m. would work because an afternoon job interview might run late. Her friend Hye-rin replied in the KakaoTalk group, “We can’t make every plan fit Chae-yeon’s timetable,” and added a laughing emoji. Two others reacted with laughing emojis too. Chae-yeon felt embarrassed; she had meant to ask, not insist. She wrote that the original time was fine and she would come if she could. Hye-rin answered with a thumbs-up, but nobody addressed the comment. On May 16, Chae-yeon passed Hye-rin outside the student union. They exchanged a quick hello and kept walking. Chae-yeon still isn’t sure whether to say that the message hurt, especially since it may have sounded like a joke to everyone else. She feels low and restless, and she has slept badly for the past two nights.

name: Oh Joon-ho
occupation: inventory coordinator at a mid-size marine-parts supplier in Busan’s Sasang-gu
topic: A dating-app match stopped responding before they could meet.
core_concern: He feels embarrassed that a brief connection mattered to him more than it apparently did to the other person.
background: Oh Joon-ho lives alone in Busan and works weekdays tracking stock and deliveries for a marine-parts supplier in Sasang-gu. On June 10, 2025, he matched with a woman on a dating app. They exchanged messages about their workdays and places to eat around Seomyeon, and on June 14 she suggested they get coffee sometime the following week. He liked having someone to message after his commute and mentioned the possible date to a coworker over lunch. By June 17, her replies had become shorter. When he asked which evening suited her, she said work was busy and then stopped replying. On June 20, he sent one brief message saying he hoped her week was going well; it remains unread. He tried putting his phone away during dinner and watched a baseball game, but kept checking the app afterward. Nothing serious had begun between them, which makes him feel foolish for telling his coworker. Tonight he is lonely, scrolling his phone without answering anyone.

name: Lee Seung-ho
occupation: Parcel delivery driver at a courier depot in Andong, covering Ok-dong routes
topic: A relative’s comment about his job has left him irritated and down.
core_concern: He worries that his family sees steady, skilled work as something he should have outgrown by 34.
background: On Saturday, 18 October 2025, Seung-ho and his wife went to her parents’ apartment in Andong for dinner. While they were clearing the table, her uncle asked whether Seung-ho was still driving for someone else at the delivery depot. He added that, at 34, Seung-ho ought to have his own delivery business by now. Two other relatives heard it, and Seung-ho felt embarrassed. His wife was in the kitchen and missed the exchange. On the drive home, she asked why he had gone quiet; he said he was tired after a week of sorting parcels and driving his route. He likes the work and had been pleased that a customer called the depot on Friday to thank him for tracking down a misaddressed parcel. That made the uncle’s remark especially irritating. On Sunday he tried to finish two delivery exception reports for Monday morning, but stopped after the first. It is Sunday evening now, the second report is still undone, and he feels deflated about going in tomorrow.

name: Bae Chan-young
occupation: Third-grade teacher at Mokpo Hadang Elementary School
topic: An awkward joke Chan-young made during an open class for parents.
core_concern: He worries that the parents now think he speaks poorly of their children when they are not around.
background: On October 23, 2025, Chan-young taught an open class with 18 parents seated along the back wall. The students were unusually quiet during a group activity, and he joked, “I wish I could borrow all of you every day; they’re never this quiet.” A few parents smiled, but one student asked whether their class was usually bad. Chan-young moved on with the lesson, though he felt his face get hot as he turned back to the board. Afterward, a fellow teacher said the class had gone well, but Chan-young was bothered that his comment could sound like a complaint about the children. On Friday, he checked the school’s parent-message app twice; there were no messages about the lesson. He started drafting a clarification, then deleted it because it seemed likely to draw attention to a remark that might have passed unnoticed. Now, at home in Mokpo, he feels mostly irritated and restless, unable to settle into anything this evening.

name: Kim Min-sung
occupation: Third-year business-information student at Jeju Jungang High School in Jeju City
topic: Not receiving a school scholarship he had applied for.
core_concern: He worries that his teacher and classmates expected him to be selected and now think less of his schoolwork.
background: Min-sung applied for his school’s first-semester alumni scholarship on May 19, 2025. The 300,000 won award would have covered accounting-certification exam fees and study materials, though his family can manage without it. His homeroom teacher had encouraged him to apply after he improved his bookkeeping score, and two classmates knew he had submitted the form. On June 5, the school posted the names of three recipients outside the staff room. His was not among them. He congratulated a classmate who received it, then felt embarrassed when someone asked whether he had checked the list. That evening, he looked over his application to see whether he had missed a requirement; he could not find one. The next day he asked his teacher if the form had been complete. It had, but the teacher did not know how the recipients had been chosen. Min-sung still has classes and exam practice to get through. Right now he feels ashamed and quiet, and he is avoiding the teacher and classmates who knew he applied.

name: Han Deok-man
occupation: Rice farmer tending two family paddies in Gilsang-myeon, Ganghwa County, Incheon
topic: A migraine made him miss a day of work in his rice fields.
core_concern: He feels embarrassed that one day of illness has left small jobs for his family to cover.
background: Deok-man grows rice in two paddies near his home in Gilsang-myeon, part of Incheon’s Ganghwa County. On July 8, 2025, he woke with a migraine and had to spend the day indoors instead of clearing weeds from the paddy banks and checking the water levels. His younger brother did the water check after Deok-man called him, but the weeding was left undone. Deok-man also missed the trip he had intended to make to Ganghwa Nonghyup for supplies. He rested in a dark room, and by the next morning the headache had eased enough for him to go outside. Nothing was damaged, but seeing the tall grass along the bank made him feel behind over a setback that should have been minor. His wife told him the work could wait a day; he took that as another reminder that she had been managing things while he lay down. The jobs are still there, and right now he feels grumpy and has been short with his wife and brother over small questions.

name: Lim Chang-ho
occupation: Owner of a fish stall at Mokpo Dongbu Market
topic: A longtime market friend got married without inviting Chang-ho.
core_concern: He worries their friendship means less to his friend than he thought, and feels embarrassed that other vendors know he was left out.
background: Chang-ho has run a fish stall at Mokpo Dongbu Market for 19 years. While arranging fish on ice each morning, he often chats with Kim Seong-bae, a former stallholder who still visits the market twice a week. On May 15, 2025, another vendor mentioned that Seong-bae was getting married on May 24 and asked whether Chang-ho would be there. Chang-ho had heard nothing about the wedding. He said he probably had to tend his stall, then noticed that two nearby vendors had received invitations by KakaoTalk. After the ceremony, someone showed him a group photo taken outside the wedding hall, with several people he knows from the market standing beside Seong-bae. He has not asked Seong-bae about it, and Seong-bae has not brought it up during his visits. Chang-ho tried to put it down to a small guest list, but that explanation feels less convincing when he sees the other vendors. As of May 29, he feels flat and unmotivated, and has skipped the evening baduk game at his neighborhood senior center that he usually enjoys.

name: Yoon Hye-won
occupation: Payroll clerk at a 65-person food-packaging company in Chuncheon’s Hupyeong Industrial Complex
topic: Hye-won feels hurt after her husband brushed off another plan to spend time together.
core_concern: She worries that making time together matters more to her than it does to her husband.
background: Hye-won handles payroll and attendance records at a food-packaging company in Chuncheon. October has been busy, so she was looking forward to a quiet Saturday with her husband: a walk around Gongjicheon and lunch afterward. They had talked about it on October 12, 2025, and she checked with him again midweek. On Friday evening, October 17, he said he had agreed to help his younger brother move some furniture on Saturday and suggested they go another time. It was the third time in a month that a plan together had slipped away. Hye-won said she understood about his brother, but when she tried to explain why she was disappointed, he called it ‘just a walk.’ She felt embarrassed by how much she had looked forward to it. On Saturday she went out alone for errands, then mentioned over dinner that she missed spending unhurried time with him. He seemed surprised and said they were together every evening, which left the point unsettled. She is tired and a bit tearful tonight, going to bed earlier than usual.

name: Lee Jin-hee
occupation: Bookkeeper at a small office-supply wholesaler in Incheon’s Yeonsu-gu, taking a barista course
topic: A training-course group member has not done his share of a short presentation.
core_concern: Jin-hee worries that asking a group member to do his share will make her seem petty, while staying quiet leaves her doing extra work.
background: On 20 May 2025, Jin-hee attended an evening barista course at a coffee academy in Incheon’s Yeonsu-gu. Her four-person group was asked to prepare a five-minute presentation on reducing café waste, due on Friday. They divided the work: Jin-hee would gather examples of milk and coffee-ground waste from their practice sessions, while another member would make two slides comparing the group’s ideas. By Thursday afternoon, his slides had not appeared in the shared file. Jin-hee asked about them twice in the KakaoTalk group chat. He replied only, ‘The rest looks good,’ leaving her unsure whether he intended to finish them. After a day reconciling invoices and receipts at the wholesaler, she stayed up late to draft the missing slides herself, but the numbers still need checking. She is irritated that the task fell to her and embarrassed by how much a small training assignment is bothering her. The presentation is tomorrow, and she has not decided what to say to the group. She feels low and restless tonight and slept badly last night.

name: Kwon So-eun
occupation: Sales associate at an Olive Young cosmetics store near Seomyeon Station in Busan
topic: So-eun lost her wallet after a shift and still has not found it.
core_concern: She is embarrassed that a small mistake has taken up so much of her time and made her ask other people to help look.
background: On July 16, 2025, So-eun finished an evening shift at the cosmetics store and stopped at a CU near Seomyeon Station. She remembers taking out her wallet to pay for a bottle of water, but did not notice it was missing until she got home. It held her ID, a transit card, and about 20,000 won. Before work the next morning, she checked her bag and coat twice, then called the store. Nothing had been turned in. She also asked a coworker to check behind the checkout counter, in case she had left it there before going out. Her coworker looked and said it was no trouble, but So-eun felt awkward having to ask during a busy sales day. She checked the Busan Metro lost-property information on her break; there was no matching report. By the evening of July 17, the wallet was still missing. She feels tired and embarrassed over something that should have been simple, and is sitting alone scrolling her phone without answering anyone on KakaoTalk.

name: Jang Da-in
occupation: Trainee hairdresser at Bom Hair, a small salon in Ok-dong, Andong
topic: She failed her driving-license road test and feels embarrassed about telling people at work.
core_concern: She worries that failing something her coworkers found easy makes her seem less capable than she wants to be.
background: Da-in started working at Bom Hair in March 2025 and has been taking driving lessons on her days off. She wants a license so she can get around Andong without always checking bus times, especially after late salon shifts. On November 20, she took the road test and scored 68, two points short of passing. She had practiced the route the weekend before, so seeing the result on the examiner’s sheet was especially frustrating. Her mother asked how it went when she got home, and Da-in said only that she had not passed. At the salon, two coworkers had wished her luck that morning; she is dreading their casual questions tomorrow more than the cost of another test. She watched part of a driving-instruction video after dinner but closed it when she stopped taking in the advice. Her combing and sectioning practice for tomorrow’s shift is still untouched. Tonight she feels tired, embarrassed, and deflated.

name: Jung Ha-rin
occupation: First-year nursing student at Ulsan College
topic: A cold is disrupting an important week of classes and assessments.
core_concern: She worries that her classmates will remember her as unreliable after she struggled through a group presentation.
background: Jung Ha-rin lives in Ulsan and is in her first year of nursing at Ulsan College. She woke up with a sore throat on Sunday, October 19, 2025, just before a week of presentations and practical assessments. By Wednesday, she was coughing into her mask between classes, but she went in because her group was presenting on hand hygiene. Halfway through her section, her voice gave out. A classmate took over the last slide while Ha-rin stood beside the screen, embarrassed and trying not to cough. Afterward, she thanked the classmate by message and got a brief “It’s okay,” but they have not spoken about it properly. Ha-rin has been drinking water and resting when she can, though she still feels unwell and has a skills assessment on Friday. She knows a cold is ordinary and the presentation was only one part of the course. Tonight, though, she is mostly irritated and restless, unable to settle into studying or anything else.

name: Choi Mal-sook
occupation: Owner of a dried-seafood shop in Chuncheon Jungang Market
topic: A strained friendship after an awkward conversation at the market.
core_concern: She is tired of her friend talking only about herself, but feels ashamed that she finally said so in front of other vendors.
background: Mal-sook has run a dried-seafood shop in Chuncheon Jungang Market for 18 years. Her friend Park Eun-hee, who runs a nearby clothing stall, often stops by after the morning rush. Lately, Eun-hee has spent those visits describing her grown son’s job search and her own disagreements with customers, rarely asking Mal-sook a question. On October 14, 2025, Mal-sook was still flustered because she had written the wrong pickup time on an order for 30 gift boxes of dried anchovies and had needed to call the customer back. She started telling Eun-hee about it while brushing dried anchovy flakes from the counter, but Eun-hee interrupted to talk about her son again. Mal-sook said, louder than she meant to, that every conversation seemed to be about Eun-hee. Two neighboring vendors heard; Eun-hee went quiet and returned to her stall. Mal-sook tried to catch her eye later, but Eun-hee looked away. The order itself is sorted out, but the exchange between them is not. Today Mal-sook feels ashamed and quiet, and is avoiding Eun-hee and the vendors who overheard.

name: Bae Young-jae
occupation: Forklift operator at an appliance-parts warehouse in Daegu’s Seongseo Industrial Complex
topic: An unresolved argument with his girlfriend after he accepted a Saturday shift.
core_concern: He worries that his girlfriend took his late notice as a sign that their time together matters less to him than work.
background: Young-jae operates a forklift at an appliance-parts warehouse in Daegu’s Seongseo Industrial Complex. On Friday, May 16, 2025, he told his girlfriend, Seo-yeon, that he had agreed to cover a Saturday shift. They had planned to have dinner in Dongseong-ro that evening, and she had already swapped her own Saturday shift at a dental clinic. At dinner, she said the extra work was not the problem; finding out only after he had agreed to it was. He felt embarrassed because he knew she had made an effort, but also annoyed that a single shift had become an argument. They finished their meal quietly and have exchanged only practical messages since. Young-jae checked his schedule to see whether he could leave early, but the Saturday deliveries needed a forklift operator, and the shift went ahead. He has not found a way to bring up the dinner again. Back at the apartment he shares with his younger brother, he feels down and has been grumpy and short with him over small things like the laundry rack.

name: Yoon Jin-hyuk
occupation: Trainee hairdresser at a small salon in Sangnam-dong, Changwon
topic: His landlord and building office keep brushing off a rattling bathroom fan.
core_concern: Jin-hyuk feels embarrassed that a small repair has become such a bother, but also annoyed that nobody seems to take him seriously.
background: Jin-hyuk started training at a salon in Sangnam-dong this spring and rents a one-room flat a short bus ride away. On June 9, 2025, the bathroom fan began making a loud plastic rattle whenever he turned it on. After a day of standing and sweeping hair at the salon, he found the noise especially irritating while getting ready for bed. He sent the building office a short video on June 11 and was told someone would check it. A staff member came by the following week, but the fan happened to be quiet during the visit. Jin-hyuk sent another message when it rattled again; the office referred him to his landlord, who replied that it sounded normal for an older fan. Nothing has been repaired. At work, Jin-hyuk keeps his annoyance to himself because the other trainees have problems of their own. This evening he feels flat and unmotivated, and he has skipped the badminton game he usually enjoys after his shift.

name: Kwon Won-jae
occupation: Front-desk clerk at a small hotel near Mokpo Station
topic: A typo in a hotel visitor guide that many guests saw.
core_concern: He worries that a visible mistake has made his coworkers doubt whether they can trust him with guest-facing notices.
background: On Friday, June 13, 2025, Won-jae updated the English visitor guide displayed on his hotel’s lobby screen. The guide listed nearby places for weekend guests, including the Mokpo Marine Cable Car. He had stayed late the previous evening to finish it after a busy check-in shift. By lunchtime, a coworker noticed that he had typed “Marien” instead of “Marine.” The screen had been running since breakfast, and more than 80 guests had checked out that morning. His coworker mentioned it during the front-desk handover, where the manager heard about it too. The manager only asked how long the guide had been displayed, but Won-jae felt his face get hot. He checked the rest of the English text twice and found no other errors, then went through the afternoon shift answering routine questions about taxis and ferry times. The typo is small, but he had been glad to be trusted with the guide and now feels embarrassed about letting it go out unchecked. It is still on the lobby screen tonight. He feels tired and a bit tearful, and is going to bed earlier than usual.

name: Oh Eun-woo
occupation: Third-year culinary arts student at Seoul Tourism High School in Gwanak-gu, doing kitchen training at a restaurant near Seoul National University Station
topic: A practice TOEIC score below the goal Eun-woo set for himself.
core_concern: He worries that the time he has spent studying English is not showing up in his results, especially when his classmates seem to be improving.
background: On Monday, 19 May 2025, Eun-woo received a 615 on the practice TOEIC he had taken in his school’s after-class English course. He had been aiming for 700 by the end of the semester, partly so he could feel more confident putting an English score on applications for hotel kitchen internships. He thought the listening section had gone well, so the result caught him off guard. When a classmate mentioned getting 720, Eun-woo congratulated him but felt embarrassed about his own score. That evening, he tried another listening exercise on the subway home through Dongjak-gu, with one earbud cutting out whenever the train doors opened. He kept losing his place and stopped before finishing it. His teacher has not yet gone through the test answers, and Eun-woo cannot tell whether he needs a different way to study or simply more practice. The setback is small, but tonight he feels low and restless. He slept badly last night and is tired again today.

name: Yang Jae-hyuk
occupation: Civil servant at the Wansan-gu District Office in Jeonju, handling resident certificate applications
topic: A stomach bug spoiled a weekend trip to Yeosu with his family.
core_concern: Jae-hyuk feels embarrassed that a short family break became extra work for his wife and a disappointment for their son.
background: Jae-hyuk took leave on Friday, July 11, 2025, so he, his wife, and their eight-year-old son could spend the weekend in Yeosu. Their son had been counting down to a visit to Aqua Planet Yeosu. Late that night, Jae-hyuk developed a stomach bug, but he hoped he would feel well enough by morning. They drove down anyway. By the time they reached their lodging, he needed to stay close to the bathroom and could not go out with them. His wife took their son for a short walk by the waterfront, then spent much of Saturday bringing Jae-hyuk water and finding something their son would eat. They drove back to Jeonju on Sunday without visiting the aquarium. At work on Monday, Jae-hyuk was feeling physically better, but a coworker’s casual question about the trip made him feel foolish. His son has since asked why they went to Yeosu if they could not see the fish. Now he is at home, still down and lonely, scrolling his phone without answering anyone.

name: Yoon Gun-woo
occupation: Junior bank teller at an iM Bank branch near Banwoldang Station in Daegu
topic: A friend shared his failed driving test with their group chat after he told him in confidence.
core_concern: He feels embarrassed in front of his friends and unsure whether he can still trust the friend he confided in.
background: Gun-woo works the customer counter at an iM Bank branch near Banwoldang Station. On July 11, 2025, he told his friend Min-jae over dinner that he had failed his driving road test for the second time. He had not told their old university friends and asked Min-jae to keep it between them. The next afternoon, while the group was arranging a weekend trip in KakaoTalk, Min-jae mentioned the test and joked that Gun-woo should not be assigned to drive. Two friends added laughing emojis, and another asked when he was trying again. Gun-woo answered the trip question but left the test comments alone. Later, he messaged Min-jae to ask why he had brought it up. Min-jae said he thought everyone would find it funny; he has not apologized. Gun-woo knows the test is something he can retake, but he is annoyed that Min-jae shared it after being asked not to. It is Sunday evening now. He feels deflated, and the updated account-opening checklist he needs to review before Monday’s shift is still unread.

name: Bae Hye-won
occupation: Owner of a small flower shop on a side street near Gaeksa in Jeonju
topic: Feeling unsettled after someone she dated a few times stopped replying
core_concern: Hye-won worries she misread their interest and feels embarrassed that she is still waiting for a reply.
background: Hye-won met Min-seok through a friend in late May 2025. They went out three times in Jeonju, most recently on June 14, when they had dinner near Gaeksa and walked together as the shops were closing. He suggested they visit an exhibition the following weekend, so on June 17 she sent a message asking which day suited him. He read it but did not answer. A second, brief message on June 20 went unanswered too. Hye-won feels more annoyed than heartbroken, but she had enjoyed their easy conversation and now feels foolish for mentioning him to her older sister. She has resisted asking their mutual friend what happened because that would make a few dates feel bigger than they were. Today she finished arranging bouquets for pickup at her flower shop near Gaeksa, then checked her phone between errands despite telling herself not to. This evening she is still irritated and restless, unable to settle into her book or the television.

name: Kang Chun-ja
occupation: Owner of a neighborhood dry cleaner in Maetan-dong, Suwon
topic: Her adult son keeps leaving the shared kitchen messy, and she is embarrassed about losing her temper.
core_concern: She worries that her frustration is making home uncomfortable for her family over something they ought to be able to settle.
background: Chun-ja lives in Suwon with her 33-year-old son. She leaves early to open her small dry-cleaning shop on a residential street in Maetan-dong, where she takes in neighbors’ shirts and coats, and comes home wanting a clear kitchen counter. Lately her son has left bowls in the sink and food containers on the table even after she has asked him to put them away. On September 18, 2025, her younger sister stopped by after dinner and saw the mess before Chun-ja had a chance to clear it. Chun-ja raised her voice at her son in front of her sister, then felt embarrassed when the room went quiet. The next evening, she washed the dishes herself but found another bowl in the sink after breakfast. She has taken a short walk around the neighborhood and tried watching television after work, but the awkwardness at home remains. Right now she feels down and ashamed of shouting, and she has been quiet around her son and avoiding her sister’s calls.

name: Song Ye-seo
occupation: Third-year student at Jeonju Girls’ High School and art-school applicant attending an evening drawing hagwon in Geumam-dong, Jeonju
topic: She sent a complaint about drawing class to the wrong KakaoTalk group.
core_concern: She worries her instructor will think she dislikes the class, when she was only tired and making a joke.
background: On Thursday, June 12, 2025, Ye-seo left her drawing hagwon after a three-hour charcoal class. While waiting for the bus in Geumam-dong, she typed a message meant for a chat with three classmates: their instructor’s “five-minute corrections” had lasted so long that she’d nearly missed the bus again. She accidentally sent it to the hagwon’s 18-person KakaoTalk group, where the instructor posts assignments. The message was still visible when she noticed the group name. Two classmates sent surprised emojis, but the instructor has not said anything, and Ye-seo has not spoken to her since. She tried working on the portfolio sketches due next week, then asked one classmate if the message sounded rude; the answer, “a little, maybe,” made her put the sketches aside. She knows it is a small mistake, but going back to class tomorrow feels awkward. At home tonight, she feels embarrassed and irritable, and has been short with her mother over a question about laundry.

name: Moon Da-in
occupation: Third-year accounting student at Incheon Girls’ Commercial High School
topic: Her score dropped on a practice exam for the computerized accounting certificate.
core_concern: She worries that doing worse after studying means she is less prepared than her classmates.
background: On September 12, 2025, Da-in got back a school practice exam for the Level 2 computerized accounting certificate. She scored 61, down from 78 on a July practice exam and below the passing mark of 70. She had spent several evenings reviewing journal entries, so the drop caught her off guard. Her teacher returned the papers individually and pointed out that most of her lost marks came from adjustment entries she had practiced before. Da-in felt embarrassed when the classmate beside her asked how it went, though she only said she’d done worse than last time. On the bus home to Bupyeong, she opened her notes and tried two similar questions, but stopped after getting one wrong. Her mother asked about the exam over dinner; Da-in said the score had dropped, and her mother told her there would be more chances to practice. That was true, but it didn’t make tonight feel easier. She feels flat and unmotivated and is skipping the Friday dance session at the neighborhood youth center that she usually enjoys.

name: Seo Seon-mi
occupation: Part-time choir conductor at a small church near Mangwon Station in Seoul
topic: Missing her mother’s birthday lunch because she had the flu.
core_concern: She feels embarrassed that her family gathered without her after she had promised to help make the day special.
background: Seon-mi conducts the choir at a small church near Mangwon Station, where she lives. On Thursday, November 13, 2025, she developed a fever after rehearsal. A neighborhood clinic confirmed she had the flu on Saturday and told her to rest at home. She missed Sunday’s service, but what bothered her more was missing her mother’s 77th birthday lunch near Gongdeok Station that afternoon. Seon-mi had arranged the reservation and promised to bring flowers; her older sister picked them up instead. A family photo appeared in their KakaoTalk group that evening, with her mother smiling between the grandchildren. Seon-mi was glad they went ahead, but embarrassed to see the empty place beside her mother. She sent a birthday message and tried calling, though coughing made the conversation brief. By Tuesday, November 18, her fever has eased, but she has not had a proper conversation with her mother about the day. She is tired and a bit tearful, and is going to bed earlier than usual.

name: Bae Jung-hwa
occupation: Math instructor at a middle-school math hagwon in Bokdae-dong, Cheongju
topic: Feeling left out of a lunch with longtime friends.
core_concern: She worries that missing one get-together means her friends have stopped thinking to include her.
background: Jung-hwa has met four friends from an old neighborhood English class for lunch every month or two for years. On May 17, 2025, she saw a photo in their KakaoTalk group chat of the other four eating lunch in Seongan-gil after visiting the Cheongju Craft Museum. Nobody had mentioned the outing to her. At their last lunch in April, she had left early to teach an evening math class, and she now wonders whether that made her seem uninterested. She sent one friend a private message saying the museum looked nice and asking how they had decided to go. The friend replied that it had come together quickly, but did not explain why Jung-hwa had not heard about it. Jung-hwa has not raised it in the group chat; she feels embarrassed that a lunch bothers her this much and annoyed that she has to ask. She was distracted while checking her students’ practice tests yesterday. She slept badly last night and feels low and restless today.

name: Son Joon-ho
occupation: Civil servant handling resident registration at Nohyeong-dong Community Service Center in Jeju City
topic: He ended a relationship and now doubts his decision.
core_concern: He worries that he gave up a good relationship because he needed more time to himself, but that contacting his former partner now would be unfair to her.
background: Joon-ho lives in Jeju City and works at the resident registration desk at Nohyeong-dong Community Service Center. He and his girlfriend, Eun-hee, had been dating for 11 months. In early June 2025, she asked whether they could keep Sunday afternoons for each other instead of deciding week by week. He had enjoyed seeing her, but between work, errands, and visits with friends, a standing arrangement felt like more than he wanted to promise. On June 12, after another discussion about it, he said they should stop dating. Eun-hee replied that she understood, and they have not met since. At first he was glad not to have a Sunday commitment. Then he noticed he missed their walks along the Tapdong waterfront and the way she sent him photographs of unusual signs she spotted around Jeju. He has drafted a message twice but deleted it because he cannot tell whether he misses her or simply dislikes the quiet. The breakup remains unresolved; tonight he feels lonely, scrolling through his phone without answering anyone.

name: Cho Do-yoon
occupation: QA tester at a small mobile-game studio in Naeoe-dong, Gimhae
topic: A coworker took credit for spotting a mismatch in a game’s release checklist.
core_concern: Do-yoon worries that if he says nothing, his careful work will keep going unnoticed, but correcting his coworker now might make him look petty.
background: Do-yoon starts at 8 a.m. at a small mobile-game studio in Naeoe-dong, Gimhae, testing builds before they are submitted to the publisher. On May 14, 2025, he noticed that two in-game item IDs did not match the release checklist and checked the issue tracker before the build went out. He told his coworker Min-jae, who helped log the mismatch for the developers. At the next morning’s handover, Min-jae told their team leader that he had caught the mismatch. The team leader thanked Min-jae in front of six people, and Do-yoon felt too embarrassed to interrupt. It was a small error, but checking those IDs had taken him most of his break. Later, he typed a correction in the team KakaoTalk chat, then deleted it because the message sounded sharper than he intended. He went through his shift as usual, though he was irritated whenever the two of them tested the same build. Nothing has been cleared up. Tonight he feels deflated, and tomorrow’s regression test report is still unfinished.

name: Kim Yu-chan
occupation: Online shopping mall product-listing assistant at a small office-supply retailer in Chuncheon's Hupyeong Industrial Complex
topic: He entered the wrong carton count for a customer order at work.
core_concern: He worries that one small error will make his coworkers think he is careless.
background: On September 18, 2025, Yu-chan was updating product listings for the office-supply retailer's online mall in Chuncheon. A small print shop had ordered 14 cartons of A4 paper, but while checking the listing, he entered 12 on the order's packing note. The fulfillment team packed only 12, and the courier had collected them by the time the office manager spotted the difference while checking the day's orders. Nothing expensive was lost, but the print shop is still short two cartons, and the discrepancy has not been sorted out. His team leader asked him to check the figures again in the morning, within earshot of two coworkers. Yu-chan felt embarrassed and annoyed with himself; he had checked the order on his screen and still typed the wrong number. On the bus home to Seoksa-dong, he tried looking at football scores to take his mind off work, but could not stay interested. This evening he is mostly irritated and restless, unable to settle into dinner or anything else.

name: Yoon Si-hoo
occupation: Banquet server at a wedding hall in Busan’s Centum City district
topic: A presentation in his evening hospitality-management class went badly.
core_concern: He worries his classmates now see him as less capable than he is at work.
background: Si-hoo works weekend wedding shifts in Centum City and takes an evening hospitality-management class at Busan Institute of Science and Technology. On October 21, 2025, his three-person group presented a plan for moving guests between a ceremony hall and a banquet room. He had prepared the section on timing, using examples from his shifts, but when the instructor asked why the plan allowed only ten minutes between groups, he mixed up two figures on the slide. He went quiet long enough for a classmate, Seo-yeon, to answer for him. After class, he checked his notes and found that the slide was right; he had simply read the wrong line. He sent the group a message saying he was sorry for freezing, then went to his next shift without looking at their replies. The mistake did not affect his job or his grade, but it feels worse because this was the part he knew firsthand. He is still ashamed and quiet, avoiding Seo-yeon and the others from the group.

name: Park Deok-man
occupation: Owner of a small hardware store in Gimhae’s Oe-dong, selling tools and household repair supplies
topic: A lingering cough has kept him off his Sunday hikes.
core_concern: He worries his friends will stop inviting him if he keeps missing the one outing he looks forward to each week.
background: Deok-man caught a cold in mid-October 2025. The fever and sore throat passed after a few days, but the cough stayed, especially when he climbed stairs or talked with customers for long. He has kept his hardware store in Oe-dong open as usual, though explaining the differences between two nearly identical door hinges left him coughing in front of a customer. On Sunday, October 19, he missed his usual walk on Bunseongsan with three friends. He expected to join them the following week, but on October 26 he was still coughing and stayed home again. A neighborhood clinic told him the lingering cough was common after a cold; he has been following its advice and taking the hills slowly when he has to carry stock. His friends sent a photo from the trail and asked how he was doing. He knows they meant well, but he felt left out. This evening he is still down about missing the walks, and he has been grumpy and short with his wife over small things at home.

name: Son Chang-ho
occupation: Owner of a small fried-chicken takeout shop in Nohyeong-dong, Jeju City
topic: An argument with a longtime friend over a small loan.
core_concern: He worries that asking for his money back has made an old friendship awkward, but staying quiet feels unfair.
background: On August 14, 2025, Chang-ho transferred 180,000 won to his friend Min-jae, who runs a side-dish stall at Jeju Dongmun Market. Min-jae was short on a supplier payment and said he would return it after the August 29 market weekend. They have known each other for years and sometimes eat together after closing their shops, so Chang-ho did not think much of lending it. When the money had not arrived by September 3, he asked about it while they were having dinner. Min-jae said the meals he had paid for recently ought to count toward what he owed. Chang-ho said he had understood those as ordinary dinners between friends, and they argued loudly enough that he felt embarrassed on the bus home. He sent a KakaoTalk message the next morning saying he had not meant to quarrel, but Min-jae has not answered or repaid him. Chang-ho is still opening his shop and filling orders. Right now he feels flat and unmotivated, and has skipped his usual evening walk along the neighborhood stream.

name: Han Young-hee
occupation: Nurse coordinating home visits at Jeju Health Center in Jeju City
topic: Trouble sleeping and concentrating at work since her mother passed away.
core_concern: She worries that missing her mother’s last call means she failed her when she was needed most.
background: Young-hee has worked at Jeju Health Center for 19 years, arranging home visits for older residents and checking in after appointments. Her 86-year-old mother lived in Seogwipo and had still been managing her own errands. On April 22, 2025, her mother called while Young-hee was finishing patient records. Young-hee meant to call back after work, but forgot. Her mother passed away unexpectedly the next morning. Young-hee and her younger brother handled the funeral arrangements together, and she returned to work after a short leave. Since then, she has slept four or five hours most nights and felt low even when she gets through her tasks. She has checked her mother’s call history several times and blames herself for that missed conversation. Her brother has said she could not have known what would happen, but it has not eased the guilt. She has tried walking along the coast after work and keeping her usual bedtime. This evening, she feels mostly irritated and restless, unable to settle into anything.

name: Jang Ok-soon
occupation: Former rice-cake maker and counter worker at Seowon Tteok in Chuncheon Jungang Market
topic: Ok-soon is struggling to look for work after being laid off.
core_concern: She worries that, at 57, she will not find another steady job and will become a burden on her family.
background: On November 3, 2025, Ok-soon was laid off from Seowon Tteok, a rice-cake stall in Chuncheon Jungang Market, after the owner combined production with a relative’s shop and cut three positions. She had spent 11 years arriving before 6 a.m. to steam rice and arrange trays of injeolmi. The sudden loss of that routine has left her shaken. Her husband still leaves for his bus-depot job at dawn; she wakes at the same hour, then lies awake thinking about their apartment fees and her mother’s care costs. She sleeps poorly, feels low most days, and blames herself for not learning other work sooner. On November 13, she went to the Chuncheon Employment Welfare Plus Center, but the openings she found required skills she does not have or commutes she cannot manage. She has kept up with meals and errands, though she has not completed another application. She has no thoughts of harming herself or wish to stop living, and no substance problem. Right now she feels down and snaps at her husband over small household things.

name: Kang Sang-woo
occupation: Electrical maintenance technician with a facilities contractor at Jeju National University Hospital
topic: Getting through work after his engagement ended.
core_concern: He worries that his mistakes over the past year drove away the person he expected to build a life with.
background: On May 7, 2025, Sang-woo’s fiancée ended their eight-year relationship and moved out of their apartment in Jeju City. Their September wedding at Maison Glad Jeju was already booked, and they have not settled the venue cancellation or the lease. He took two days off, then returned to his electrical maintenance shifts at Jeju National University Hospital. He still completes his inspections, but has to check his notes twice because he is sleeping only four or five hours a night. His mother called after hearing the news from a relative; he told her he was managing, then felt guilty for making her worry. He has tried walking after work and keeping his usual bedtime, without much change. He blames himself for working late through the winter and missing conversations his fiancée had wanted to have. He has no thoughts of harming himself or wishing he were not here. Right now he feels flat and unmotivated, and he has skipped his Saturday badminton games for two weeks.

name: Nam Ji-hye
occupation: Resident-services clerk at the management office of a 620-unit apartment complex in Suseong-gu, Daegu
topic: A criminal complaint filed against her after a resident’s fall in an apartment stairwell.
core_concern: She fears that a maintenance request she failed to follow up may have contributed to a resident’s passing away.
background: Ji-hye handles residents’ calls and enters repair requests at the management office of an apartment complex in Suseong-gu. On May 26, 2025, a resident reported that a stairwell light was flickering. Ji-hye entered the request, but the maintenance worker assigned to it was out that day, and she did not check whether anyone else had taken it over. Two evenings later, an older resident fell in that stairwell and later passed away. On June 9, his daughter filed a criminal complaint alleging that the office had ignored warnings about the light; Ji-hye’s name appears on the request record. She gave the police a copy of the record and explained what she remembered, but she has not heard what will happen next. The daughter’s account of the unanswered request has stayed with her. Ji-hye still goes to work and answers residents’ calls, though she checks each new entry several times. Her sleep has been poor, and she keeps blaming herself for not making one more call. Tonight she feels tired and a bit tearful, and she is going to bed earlier than usual.

name: Moon Sang-woo
occupation: forklift operator and co-owner of a small freight-handling business in Daejeon’s Daehwa-dong industrial area
topic: His freight-handling business is closing this month, leaving him with large debts.
core_concern: He blames himself for the closure and fears he cannot meet the debts he personally guaranteed.
background: Moon Sang-woo has spent eleven years unloading trucks and moving pallets at the freight-handling business he ran with his father in Daejeon’s Daehwa-dong industrial area. His father passed away on August 2, 2025. Nine days later, their largest customer ended its contract after cutting its own warehouse operations. On August 18, Moon told their two employees that the business would close by August 29. He still goes in each morning to finish outstanding jobs, but the empty loading bays make the decision feel final. The equipment loan and overdue rent total about 78 million won, much of it backed by his personal guarantee. He has spoken with Shinhan Bank about the loan and gathered documents for the Credit Counseling and Recovery Service, but neither step has settled what he owes. His wife knows the business is closing; he has not yet shown her the full balance. He has no thoughts of harming himself, no wish not to be alive, and no substance problem. Right now he feels low and restless, blames himself for not protecting the business, and has slept badly for the past two nights.

name: Lim Geum-ja
occupation: Rice-cake seller at a stall in Yeosu’s Seogyo Market
topic: A fight with her older brother after their mother passed away.
core_concern: Geum-ja fears that her brother’s decision to cut contact is permanent and blames herself for losing their relationship.
background: Geum-ja runs a rice-cake stall at Yeosu’s Seogyo Market, starting the steamer before 6 a.m. and supplying two nearby side-dish shops. On September 24, 2025, her mother passed away after a short admission to Suncheon St. Carollo Hospital. During the funeral, Geum-ja’s older brother accused her of keeping him out of decisions about their mother’s care, although she had forwarded hospital updates to their family KakaoTalk room. On September 29, a dispute over the remaining hospital bill turned into shouting in front of their cousins. He told her not to contact him again and blocked her number. She sent one message through his daughter to clarify what she had paid; there has been no reply. With Chuseok orders due, she still opened the stall every morning and packed songpyeon, but she has slept poorly and blames herself for the fight. She has no thoughts of ending her life, no wish to be gone, no urge or plan to harm herself, and no substance problem. Right now she feels lonely, scrolling her phone without answering anyone.

name: Heo Joon-ho
occupation: Purchasing coordinator at a mid-size industrial-parts supplier in Pohang
topic: Returning to work after reporting an assault by a former coworker.
core_concern: He worries the report will make work harder for everyone and blames himself for not leaving sooner.
background: Joon-ho handles purchase orders for a parts supplier near Pohang’s steelworks. On October 8, 2025, a former coworker who had been arguing with him about an unpaid expense claim waited outside the office after closing. The man shoved Joon-ho against a wall and threatened him when he said he would call the police. Joon-ho had bruising on his shoulder and reported the assault to Pohang Nambu Police Station two days later. His manager knows, but the claim still appears in their shared records, and Joon-ho dreads seeing the man’s name during the workday. He has tried taking a different bus home and keeping his attention on routine orders. Neither has helped much. He sleeps in short stretches, feels low most mornings, and keeps blaming himself for having answered the man outside. He has no thoughts of harming himself and is still going to work. Tonight he feels deflated, with tomorrow’s supplier reconciliation unfinished.

name: Shin Yu-jin
occupation: QA intern at a six-person mobile-game studio near Wonju Innovation City
topic: Yu-jin is struggling after learning she may lose her jeonse deposit to rental fraud.
core_concern: She blames herself for trusting the landlord and fears she will be left owing the bank for a home she can no longer keep.
background: On 6 May 2025, when Yu-jin’s lease ended, her landlord failed to return her ₩68 million jeonse deposit. Another tenant told her the building was headed to auction, and the real-estate agent who handled her contract had closed his office. She had checked the property register before signing in 2023; seeing a lien added later left her blaming herself for not checking it again. ₩42 million of the deposit came from a youth housing loan, and the bank still expects payments. On 9 May, she filed a report at Wonju Police Station and took her contract to the Korea Legal Aid Corporation’s Wonju office, but she has no answer yet about recovering the money. She still goes to her QA internship and marks bugs in the studio’s mobile game, though poor sleep makes it hard to concentrate. Her sister has offered a spare room, but Yu-jin has not packed. She has no thoughts of harming herself. This evening she feels mostly irritated and restless, unable to settle into anything.

name: Park Jin-woo
occupation: forklift operator at an auto-parts warehouse in Jeonju’s Palbok-dong industrial area
topic: He is struggling to keep up with work after his divorce was finalized.
core_concern: He blames himself for the end of his marriage and fears that his relationship with his daughter will become distant.
background: Jin-woo’s divorce was finalized at Jeonju District Court on May 19, 2025. He and his former wife had lived apart since winter, but signing the final papers left him shaken. Their eight-year-old daughter now lives with her mother in Iksan. The arrangement says Jin-woo can see her twice a month, though they have not settled the next visit. He still wakes at 5:40 for his warehouse shift, checks pallet labels and drives the forklift, but he has been sleeping only a few hours and sometimes has to read a work order twice. At home, the empty space where his daughter kept her schoolbag is hard to look at. He tried keeping his usual evening walk along the Jeonjucheon, then stopped after a few nights because he could not stop blaming himself for arguments during the marriage. He has no thoughts of harming himself. Right now he feels low, ashamed and quiet, and is avoiding calls from his former wife and her family.

name: Hwang Eun-woo
occupation: Junior bank teller at an NH NongHyup Bank branch in Wonju
topic: Eun-woo has barely slept and is having panic attacks after a car accident.
core_concern: He worries that he caused lasting harm to another driver and cannot face the people waiting for answers.
background: On November 12, 2025, Eun-woo was driving home through Wonju after staying late to close the teller counter. At an intersection near Wonju Intercity Bus Terminal, his car collided with another car. The other driver was taken to hospital with a fractured collarbone; Eun-woo was checked and sent home. The police are still reviewing what happened, and the insurer has asked him for another statement. He keeps blaming himself, though he does not yet know how the collision will be assessed. For the past week he has slept only a few hours a night. Twice, the sound of brakes outside his apartment brought on a racing heart and trembling that took a long time to settle. He has still gone to work, but he asked a colleague to handle customers when his hands shook over a deposit slip. He has no thoughts of harming himself, but his mood has stayed low. Right now he feels ashamed and quiet, and he is avoiding his colleague’s questions and calls from the other driver’s insurer.
